questions.title: Range Sum Query - Immutable
questions.inputFormat: The first line contains the space-separated elements of nums. The second line contains q. Each of the next q lines contains "sumRange left right".
questions.outputFormat: Print the sum for every sumRange operation on a new line.
questions.constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 10^4
-10^5 <= nums[i] <= 10^5
0 <= left <= right < nums.length
At most 10^4 sumRange calls will be made.

questions.title: Range Sum Query - Mutable
questions.inputFormat: The first line contains the space-separated elements of nums. The second line contains q. Each of the next q lines is either "update index val" or "sumRange left right".
questions.outputFormat: For every sumRange operation, print the resulting sum on a new line.
questions.constraints:
1 <= nums.length <= 3 * 10^4
-100 <= nums[i], val <= 100
0 <= index < nums.length
0 <= left <= right < nums.length
At most 3 * 10^4 update and sumRange calls will be made.

questions.title: Queue Reconstruction by Height
questions.statement:
You are given an array \`people\` describing people in a queue, in arbitrary order. Each \`people[i] = [hi, ki]\` represents a person of height \`hi\` with exactly \`ki\` people in front of them whose height is greater than or equal to \`hi\`.

Reconstruct and return the queue. The result must be formatted as an array where \`queue[j] = [hj, kj]\` is the person at position \`j\`.

### Example 1

**Input:** \`people = [[7, 0], [4, 4], [7, 1], [5, 0], [6, 1], [5, 2]]\`

**Output:** \`[[5, 0], [7, 0], [5, 2], [6, 1], [4, 4], [7, 1]]\`

**Explanation:** In the reconstructed queue, each person has exactly the required number of people of at least their height before them.

### Example 2

**Input:** \`people = [[6, 0], [5, 0], [4, 0], [3, 2], [2, 2], [1, 4]]\`

**Output:** \`[[4, 0], [5, 0], [2, 2], [3, 2], [1, 4], [6, 0]]\`
questions.inputFormat: The first line contains n. Each of the next n lines contains hi and ki for one person.
questions.outputFormat: Print the reconstructed queue as n lines, each containing hi and ki.
questions.constraints:
1 <= people.length <= 2000
0 <= hi <= 10^6
0 <= ki < people.length
The queue can be reconstructed.
